purpose: Sync HTTP orchestrator that turns a Customer's cart + chosen address into (a) a server-priced preview and (b) a transactionally-safe Order + reservation + payment-intent triple. Owns NO order rows and NO payment rows — orchestrates Cart, Identity, Catalog, Inventory, Order, Payment via sync HTTP calls and uses sequential compensating actions on failure (no 2PC). Refactored from v0.1 to (a) wire buyerEmail via identity.profile.read step 2 (REV-L2-001 closure), (b) make the INFLIGHT race fix explicit via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING (TryClaimOrLookup pattern; closes dry-run #1 H02), (c) reaffirm pricing.go as the §11.2 single source, and (d) tighten the compensation matrix to the contracts-locked 3-retry [50,200,800]ms backoff.

idempotency_flow.scope: per-(endpoint='checkout.commit', customerUserId=claims.sub) — a single key cannot be reused across two different customers (defense against accidental cross-tenant collision).
idempotency_flow.request_hash_algorithm: sha256(canonicalize(request_body))  where canonicalize sorts JSON keys, normalises whitespace, lowercases hex, and EXCLUDES the Authorization header but INCLUDES the shippingAddressId.
idempotency_flow.atomic_claim_pattern_LOCKED: TryClaimOrLookup — single statement: `INSERT INTO checkout.idempotency_keys (key, customer_user_id, request_hash, status, ...) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,'INFLIGHT',...) ON CONFLICT (key, customer_user_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING key`. If the INSERT returns a row, the caller is the winner; if it returns 0 rows, run a follow-up `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` to inspect the existing row's status. This single-statement insert closes the dry-run #1 H02 race window where a Lookup→InsertInflight pair could both observe NOT FOUND and both proceed (two orders for one Idempotency-Key). PK = (key, customer_user_id).
lookup_branches_after_TryClaimOrLookup: winner=true → caller proceeds to orchestration (own the INFLIGHT row).
winner=false, existing.status=COMPLETED, existing.request_hash MATCHES → return cached response_envelope verbatim with cached http_status. Do NOT re-execute side-effects.
winner=false, existing.status=COMPLETED, existing.request_hash MISMATCHES → return 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED with data={originalOrderId} extracted from the cached envelope.
winner=false, existing.status=INFLIGHT → return 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INFLIGHT with header `Retry-After: 1`.
winner=false, existing.status=ABANDONED → DELETE the dead row and re-INSERT (the row lock from FOR UPDATE means our re-insert wins); proceed to orchestration as a fresh attempt.
idempotency_flow.persistence_pattern: The 'INFLIGHT' insert + final 'COMPLETED' update wrap the entire orchestration. If the process crashes between step 6 and step 10, the row stays INFLIGHT until either (a) a retry overwrites it (after the janitor sweeps stale INFLIGHT > 60s into ABANDONED) OR (b) the 24h TTL elapses. See janitor below.
idempotency_flow.janitor: Background goroutine in checkout (started at boot per main.go runJanitor): every 60s, runs `UPDATE checkout.idempotency_keys SET status='ABANDONED', response_envelope=<UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT envelope>, http_status=504 WHERE key IN (SELECT key FROM checkout.idempotency_keys WHERE status='INFLIGHT' AND created_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '60 seconds' LIMIT 100 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)`. Subsequent retries with the same key see ABANDONED and re-claim (delete + insert). Operator can purge ABANDONED rows manually if a fresh attempt is desired.

if err != nil: ROLLBACK; return 503 DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE

COMPLETED + hashMismatch → ROLLBACK; return 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED { originalOrderId }
INFLIGHT → ROLLBACK; set Retry-After:1; return 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INFLIGHT
ABANDONED → DELETE the row; re-INSERT INFLIGHT (we hold the FOR UPDATE lock); fall through as winner

if profile failed: finalize(UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT); COMMIT; return

// ---- Step 5 — server-side pricing snapshot + orderId mint ----
orderId = uuidv7()                                                 // doubles as Idempotency-Key for steps 6/7/8
subtotal = sum(line.priceSnapshot * line.qty)                      // int64 minor units

{orderId, items, expiresAt: now+15min, idempotencyKey: orderId})  // timeout 1.5s, 1 retry
// Order is sole writer (ADR-003). Idempotent on orderId. Carries buyerEmail (REV-L2-001).
items: lineItems, subtotal, shippingFee, couponDiscount: 0, total})  // timeout 1s, 1 retry
// Reservation TTL (15min) is the safety net; saga reconciler will surface DEGRADED rows.

// (B) release reservation — 3 retries with exp backoff

// Reservation TTL safety net; events.reservation.expired drives PAYMENT_EXPIRED via Order's state-driven consumer.

endpoints.distributed_tx_pattern: Sequential sync HTTP with explicit per-step compensating actions per ADR-007. NOT 2PC. Rationale: (a) all downstream services are sync HTTP and idempotent on a Checkout-generated key (orderId); (b) the only durable state Checkout owns is the idempotency_keys row, which holds the final outcome envelope so retries are deterministic; (c) the inventory reservation TTL (15min, cross-cutting.pricing.constants.RESERVATION_TTL_MINUTES) is the absolute safety net for any compensation-failure scenario.
failure_modes: VALIDATION_ERROR (400) — empty cart (CHK-001), missing/invalid Idempotency-Key, client-priced fields present (CHK-005), couponCode present (CHK-AMBIG-002)
INSUFFICIENT_STOCK (409) — pre-reservation OR reservation-race (CHK-004); per-item details {productId, requestedQty, availableQty}
IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED (409) — same key, different request_hash (CHK-009); data carries originalOrderId
IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INFLIGHT (409) — concurrent same-key call still running (CHK-009); header Retry-After: 1
DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE (503) — checkout DB or any downstream's DB
UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT (504) — any downstream exceeded its budget after retry

persistence.transaction_boundaries: Single Postgres tx (ReadCommitted) wraps the idempotency_keys row read/insert/update across the entire orchestration. Downstream HTTP calls happen INSIDE the open tx (the row lock holds INFLIGHT). saga_log INSERT is in the same tx. Tx commits at step 10 (success) or at any decided-error step that wrote a final envelope to the row. Compensation calls happen on context.Background() so a client cancel does not abort an in-flight reservation.release.
persistence.negative_invariants: Checkout MUST NOT write to orders, order_items, payment_intents, stock_levels, reservations. Enforced by absence of those tables in the checkout schema (ADR-001 schema-per-service); cross-service joins forbidden by cross-cutting.persistence.

common_modules_referenced: common/middleware/internal_auth — recipient-side X-Internal-Secret with crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare (ADR-008). NOTE: Checkout is the CALLER for the four internal hops, not the recipient — but it MUST send the X-Internal-Secret header populated from os.Getenv("INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET") on every internal call.

timeouts_and_retries_summary.rationale: PERF-002 caps checkout p95 at 500ms in local Docker Compose. Per-call budgets aggregate to ~5s under worst-case retry; success path with no retries is well under 500ms (estimated ~150–300ms p95 across 6 sequential + 1 parallel-fanout calls). Step 2 (identity.profile.read) adds ~50–100ms in the success path and is required for REV-L2-001 buyerEmail wire.

metrics: checkout_compensation_failed_total{step}  // alert >=1 over 5min — DEGRADED row in saga_log
checkout_saga_degraded_unreconciled_total  // saga reconciler emits when DEGRADED rows are >1h old (REV-L2-008)
observability.logs: Structured JSON via slog; every step logs {orderId?, customerUserId, traceId, step, durationMs, outcome}. Compensation-failure logs at level=CRITICAL with the inner err string. NEVER logs Authorization or X-Internal-Secret values.
observability.tracing: W3C traceparent propagated to every downstream call; spans named checkout.commit.<step>. The customer's incoming traceparent header is preserved end-to-end.

security_notes: claims.sub authoritative: customerUserId NEVER read from request body.
Idempotency-Key scoped per (endpoint, customerUserId) prevents cross-tenant collision attacks.
Server-side price authority (CHK-005) enforced at request-validation AND at step 5 snapshot — defense in depth.
Address ownership enforced via identity.address.list (caller-scoped) — no direct address-id lookup that could be IDOR'd.

The customer JWT is forwarded only to identity.profile.read (step 2), identity.address.list (step 3), cart.read (step 1), and cart.clear-on-checkout (step 9) — the four customer-context hops. Steps 6/7/8 + compensations use X-Internal-Secret only; the JWT is NOT forwarded into Inventory/Order/Payment.

X-Internal-Secret loaded from os.Getenv("INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET") at boot (ADR-008 LOCKED env-var name); MIN 32 bytes; refuse to start if shorter or absent. Comma-separated rotation overlap supported (try each segment).
No PII written to logs. customerUserId is acceptable per cross-cutting.persistence; never log addresses, names, or email.
